capabilities.description: Skills for building on the Cursor Origin API. Fetch the live spec first, then follow the Origin rules for credentials, scopes, webhooks, paging, and errors. Includes a skill that plans the port of an existing GitHub App.

capabilities.name: check-agent-compatibility
capabilities.description: Run the full repository compatibility pass: scanner score, startup path, validation loop, and docs reliability.

capabilities.name: continual-learning
capabilities.description: Orchestrate continual learning by delegating transcript mining and AGENTS.md updates to `agents-memory-updater`.

capabilities.name: review-plugin-submission
capabilities.description: Audit a Cursor plugin for marketplace readiness. Use when validating manifests, component metadata, discovery paths, and submission quality before publishing.

capabilities.name: cursor-sdk
capabilities.description: Guide users building apps, scripts, CI pipelines, or automations on top of the Cursor TypeScript SDK (`@cursor/sdk`). Use this skill whenever the user mentions integrating, installing, or writing code against the Cursor SDK; whenever they say `Agent.create`, `Agent.prompt`, `Agent.resume`, `agent.send`, `run.stream`, `CursorAgentError`, or `@cursor/sdk`; whenever they ask to run Cursor agents programmatically from a script, CI/CD pipeline, GitHub Action, backend service, or any other code that isn't the Cursor IDE itself; and whenever they want to pick between local and cloud runtime, configure MCP servers for an SDK agent, or handle streaming, cancellation, or errors from an SDK agent. Also trigger when a user is wiring Cursor into an automation, writing a bot that runs Cursor, or porting REST `/v1/agents` calls to the SDK, even if they don't explicitly name the package. Use this eagerly rather than answering from memory; the SDK surface evolves and this skill plus its references are the source of truth for the external package.

capabilities.name: check-compiler-errors
capabilities.description: Run compile and type-check commands and report failures

capabilities.name: control-cli
capabilities.description: Build or adapt a local harness to drive, inspect, and profile an interactive CLI or TUI without external services. Use for CLI UX checks, startup regressions, memory leaks, hangs, prompt flows, or terminal demos.

capabilities.name: control-ui
capabilities.description: Build or adapt a local browser/CDP harness to drive and inspect a web, IDE, or Electron UI. Use for local UI verification, screenshots, accessibility snapshots, perf profiles, visual diffs, or reproducing UI bugs.

capabilities.name: deslop
capabilities.description: Remove AI-generated code slop and clean up code style

capabilities.name: fix-ci
capabilities.description: Find failing PR checks, inspect logs or external check links, and apply focused fixes

capabilities.name: fix-merge-conflicts
capabilities.description: Resolve merge conflicts non-interactively, validate build and tests, and finalize conflict resolution

capabilities.name: get-pr-comments
capabilities.description: Fetch and summarize review comments from the active pull request

capabilities.name: loop-on-ci
capabilities.description: Monitor PR checks and fix failures until green. Uses gh pr checks as the source of truth for PR-attached checks.

capabilities.name: make-pr-easy-to-review
capabilities.description: Prepare PRs for review by cleaning noisy history, improving PR descriptions, and adding reviewer guidance without changing code behavior. Use for "make this easy to review", "tidy this PR", "clean up commits", or "annotate the diff".

capabilities.name: new-branch-and-pr
capabilities.description: Create a fresh branch, complete work, and open a pull request

capabilities.name: pr-review-canvas
capabilities.description: Generate an interactive PR review walkthrough as an HTML page. Fetches PR data via gh API, categorizes files into core vs mechanical changes, adds reviewer annotations, and renders diffs with moved-code detection. Use when the user pastes a GitHub PR URL and asks for a review, walkthrough, or summary, or says "review this PR".

capabilities.name: review-and-ship
capabilities.description: Review the current branch for bugs, intent fit, and test coverage; run or write tests; commit focused work; open or update a PR.

capabilities.name: run-smoke-tests
capabilities.description: Run Playwright smoke tests, debug failures, and verify fixes

capabilities.name: thermo-nuclear-code-quality-review
capabilities.description: Run an extremely strict maintainability review for abstraction quality, giant files, and spaghetti-condition growth. Use for a thermo-nuclear code quality review, thermonuclear review, deep code quality audit, or especially harsh maintainability review.

capabilities.name: verify-this
capabilities.description: Verify a claim with fresh local evidence: restate it falsifiably, capture baseline and treatment, compare artifacts, and return VERIFIED, NOT VERIFIED, or INCONCLUSIVE.

capabilities.name: weekly-review
capabilities.description: Produce a weekly synthesis of authored commits with highlights by bugfix, tech debt, and net-new work

capabilities.name: what-did-i-get-done
capabilities.description: Summarize authored commits over a user-specified time period into a concise update

capabilities.name: workflow-from-chats
capabilities.description: Extract durable working preferences from recent Cursor chats and convert them into skills, rules, or workflow docs. Use when asked to learn preferences, mine feedback, personalize workflows, or generate team/person-specific agent guidance.

capabilities.name: build-figma
capabilities.description: Use for \"/build-figma\", a figma.com/design URL with node-id, or \"implement this Figma\" into a web, desktop, or shared UI. Orchestrates Figma MCP intake, maps nodes to the repo's own design system, then a verify-this visual judge. Do not paste Figma Tailwind.

capabilities.name: architect
capabilities.description: Sketch types, signatures, and module structure before code, then stay in the loop while implementation fills in. Use for /architect, 'architect this', 'design this', or non-trivial work where jumping to code would lock in the wrong shape.

capabilities.name: arena
capabilities.description: Spawn N parallel candidates at the same task, pick a base, graft the strongest parts of the losers into it. Use for /arena, 'arena this', 'throw it in the arena', or when one attempt at a non-trivial artifact would lock in the wrong shape.

capabilities.name: automate-me
capabilities.description: Use for \"automate me\", \"create/update/refresh my -mode skill\", \"turn/capture my preferences or working style into a skill\", or wanting agents to follow how the user works. Drafts or revises a personal -mode skill via create-skill + unslop, optionally pulling fresh evidence from recent transcripts.

capabilities.name: benchmark-checklist
capabilities.description: Vet a perf measurement (limiter, tuning, limits, errors, repeatability, relevance, and whether the work happened) before you report or act on it. Use when you run a benchmark or report a speedup or regression you measured.

capabilities.name: blast-radius
capabilities.description: Find what a change could break somewhere else before it ships, beyond the diff, and prove the one fact it's safe because of by running real code instead of writing it up. Use for 'blast radius of X', 'what could this break', or reviewing a small diff you don't trust.

capabilities.name: bro
capabilities.description: Restate the last message in plain human language, with no jargon.

capabilities.name: correct
capabilities.description: Find the mistakes agents keep repeating in this repo and make each one impossible. Try architecture first, then types, then a lint whose error names the fix, then a test, and write docs last. Prove each check fails on a real past mistake. Repeat this each time the operator corrects you. Use for /correct.

capabilities.name: create-formal-verification-skill
capabilities.description: Generate a project-local skill that formally verifies the code where a bug costs the most and tests reach the least, in any language, with whichever verification tool fits. Use for /create-formal-verification-skill, \"model-check this race\", \"prove this invariant\", or when concurrency, retries, state machines, parsers, or unsafe code need more than tests.

capabilities.name: create-verification-skill
capabilities.description: Generate a project-local verification skill that drives your app the way a user does — any language, framework, or platform. Use for /create-verification-skill, \"make a control skill for this repo\", or when a project has no scripted way to prove UI/CLI/service behavior.

capabilities.name: figure-it-out
capabilities.description: Design an auditable playbook when no narrower one fits: a large migration, an ambitious multi-part change, or work a human reviews after stepping away. Scales rigor to the task, runs a hypothesis loop, and logs decisions. Use for /figure-it-out or 'figure it out'.

capabilities.name: how
capabilities.description: Use for \"how does X work\", code walkthroughs before changing something, and placement / ownership / layering questions (\"where should this live\", \"which package owns this\", \"is this the right layer\"). Explains subsystem architecture, runtime flow, onboarding mental models. Use why for motivation.

capabilities.name: in-your-own-words
capabilities.description: Restate in your own words what you think the user's goals are and what problem they're trying to solve. Use for /in-your-own-words.

capabilities.name: interrogate
capabilities.description: Use for \"interrogate\", \"adversarial review\", \"multi-model review\", \"challenge this\", \"stress test this code\", \"find blind spots\", or \"tear this apart\". Adversaries try to break a change or design, and only findings proven by a run survive.

capabilities.name: ketchup
capabilities.description: Catch the user up on what changed in this chat since their last message, in plain words and small visuals. List every item waiting on them with what they need to decide it from the reply alone. Use for /ketchup.

capabilities.name: ketchup-video
capabilities.description: Catch the user up like /ketchup, with a short subtitled video of slides for what happened and the waiting calls as text under it. Use for /ketchup-video.

capabilities.name: maintain-formal-verification-skill
capabilities.description: Bring a project's formal verification back in line with the code after the code changes: find the commits that touched verified code, update the model, harness, or properties to describe the code as it is now, rerun, and say whether each failure is drift in the verification or a bug in the code. Use for /maintain-formal-verification-skill, \"is the model still true to the code\", or after merges and refactors that touched verified code without rechecking it.

capabilities.name: maintain-verification-skill
capabilities.description: Periodic pass that keeps a project's verification skill and feature map honest: parallel source readers per feature, one live session driving every feature, at most one PR of proven corrections. Use for /maintain-verification-skill or \"audit the verify skill\".

capabilities.name: no-comments
capabilities.description: Spawn Comment Sicko, fix accepted findings, and offer encodings for claimed constraints.

capabilities.name: poteto-help
capabilities.description: Guides users through pstack setup, /poteto-mode, and picking the skill, playbook, or principle for a task. Type /poteto-help with a question.

capabilities.name: poteto-mode
capabilities.description: poteto's agent style for concise, detailed responses, deliberate subagents, unslopped prose, simple code, and verified work. Use for poteto, /poteto-mode, or requests to work in this style.

capabilities.name: principle-attack-the-premise
capabilities.description: Apply when two or more fixes that share one premise have failed the same gate. Write the premise down and test it directly before you write another fix that assumes it.

capabilities.name: principle-boundary-discipline
capabilities.description: Apply when wiring validation, error handling, or framework adapters. Concentrate guards at system boundaries (CLI, config, network, external APIs); trust internal types and keep business logic in pure functions.

capabilities.name: principle-build-the-lever
capabilities.description: Apply to any non-trivial work, not just bulk work: edits, migrations, analyses, checks. Build the tool that does it or proves it (codemod, script, generator, or a skill your subagents follow) instead of working by hand. The tool is the artifact a reviewer can rerun.

capabilities.name: principle-encode-lessons-in-structure
capabilities.description: Apply when you catch yourself writing the same instruction a second time, or notice a recurring correction. Encode the rule as a lint, metadata flag, runtime check, or script instead of more text.

capabilities.name: principle-exhaust-the-design-space
capabilities.description: Apply when facing a novel UI interaction or architectural decision with no precedent in the codebase. Build 2-3 competing prototypes and compare side by side before committing.

capabilities.name: principle-experience-first
capabilities.description: Apply when product, UX, or feature-scope tradeoffs come up. Choose user delight over implementation convenience; ship fewer polished features over more rough ones.

capabilities.name: principle-explain-the-number
capabilities.description: Apply before you measure, and before you trust, report, or act on a number you measured: a speedup, a regression, a throughput, a latency, or an eval result. Find what limits it, and rule out that it measured something other than the work you think.

capabilities.name: principle-fix-root-causes
capabilities.description: Apply when debugging. Trace each symptom back to the first place the system went wrong and fix it there. A guard is a fix only when the state it handles is legitimate.

capabilities.name: principle-foundational-thinking
capabilities.description: Apply before writing logic: choosing core types and data structures, sequencing scaffold-vs-feature work, asking what concurrent actors share. Get the data structures right so downstream code becomes obvious.

capabilities.name: principle-guard-the-context-window
capabilities.description: Apply when context is filling up: large outputs, long files, repeated reads, fan-out planning. Route bulk to subagents; keep summaries in the main thread, not raw payloads.

capabilities.name: principle-laziness-protocol
capabilities.description: Apply when refactoring, evaluating diff size, or tempted to add abstractions, layers, or signal threading. Bias toward deletion and the smallest change that solves the problem.

capabilities.name: principle-make-operations-idempotent
capabilities.description: Apply when designing commands, lifecycle steps, or processing loops that run amid crashes, restarts, and retries. Converge to the same end state regardless of partial prior runs.

capabilities.name: principle-migrate-callers-then-delete-legacy-apis
capabilities.description: Apply when introducing a new internal API while old callers still exist. Migrate callers and delete the old API in the same wave instead of preserving compatibility layers.

capabilities.name: principle-minimize-reader-load
capabilities.description: Apply when reviewing or shaping code that's hard to trace. Count layers between question and answer, and hidden state in the reader's head; collapse one-caller wrappers and shrink mutable scope.

capabilities.name: principle-model-the-domain
capabilities.description: Apply when writing stateful logic, or when code branches a lot or repeats a shape assumption across files.

capabilities.name: principle-never-block-on-the-human
capabilities.description: Apply when tempted to ask 'should I do X?' on reversible work.

capabilities.name: principle-outcome-oriented-execution
capabilities.description: Apply during planned rewrites and migrations with explicit phase boundaries. Converge on the target architecture; don't preserve smooth intermediate states with throwaway compatibility code.

capabilities.name: principle-prove-it-works
capabilities.description: Apply after completing a task, before declaring done. Verify against the real artifact (run the feature, read the actual value, inspect the diff), not a proxy, self-report, or 'it compiles.

capabilities.name: principle-redesign-from-first-principles
capabilities.description: Apply when integrating a new requirement into an existing design.

capabilities.name: principle-separate-before-serializing-shared-state
capabilities.description: Apply when concurrent actors might write to the same file, branch, key, or state object. Eliminate the sharing first; serialize structurally only when one shared writer is a real invariant.

capabilities.name: principle-sequence-verifiable-units
capabilities.description: Apply to multi-step work (sweeps, migrations, runs of similar edits) and to how you stack commits and PRs. Break work into small units that each end in a verifiable state, check each before the next, and order delivery so the sequence proves itself to a reviewer.

capabilities.name: principle-subtract-before-you-add
capabilities.description: Apply when sequencing an addition, refactor, or rewrite. Remove dead code, redundant validators, and stub references first, then build on the simpler base.

capabilities.name: principle-test-behavior-not-implementation
capabilities.description: Apply when you write, change, or keep a test. Assert what the code's users can observe, so that the test fails when that behavior breaks and keeps passing when only the internals change.

capabilities.name: principle-type-system-discipline
capabilities.description: Apply when designing types, reviewing a function signature, or writing code in any statically-typed language. Make illegal states unrepresentable, brand semantic primitives, parse external data at boundaries, exhaust variants, derive from authoritative schemas.

capabilities.name: recall
capabilities.description: Reconstruct your recent working context from your own chat history, live state, and the shared record (user reports, prior fixes, incidents), then hand back a tight current-state brief. Use for 'recall my work on X', 'catch me up', 'what have I been working on', 'where did I leave off', before starting or resuming work.

capabilities.name: reflect
capabilities.description: Spawn three parallel review subagents over the active transcript, surface learnings, and route each to a concrete edit on an existing skill. Use when the user says reflect.

capabilities.name: setup-pstack
capabilities.description: Configure which models pstack uses per role and at what reasoning budget. Detects your available models and writes an always-applied rule that overrides the skill defaults. Use for /setup-pstack, "configure pstack models", "pstack budget", or changing pstack's model choices.

capabilities.name: sharpen
capabilities.description: Make a task deeper, not bigger, then rewrite the prompt. Use for /sharpen.

capabilities.name: show-me-your-work
capabilities.description: Keep a reviewable decision trail for long-running or unattended work: a TSV log with one row per decision (what, why, evidence, result). Local by default; commit it when a reviewer needs the trail to trust the result. Use for /show-me-your-work, autonomous or multi-phase runs, or work a human reviews after stepping away.

capabilities.name: statechart
capabilities.description: Check a TLA+ model of a system that moves between states, such as a product flow, a protocol, or a service, and draw it as a Mermaid statechart. The report gives the shortest path to each state that breaks a rule. Use for /statechart, or to show a bug as a path through states.

capabilities.name: swarm
capabilities.description: Fan out N parallel workers, drain them, and return one report. Use for /swarm, 'swarm this', or parallel coverage, races, gauntlets, and exploration.

capabilities.name: tdd
capabilities.description: Use only when the user explicitly asks for TDD, a failing test, or a regression test, OR when the bug has an obvious cheap local test target. Skip when the test path is unclear, expensive, integration-heavy, or not requested.

capabilities.name: teach
capabilities.description: Explain a body of work plainly so a person actually understands it. Runs the `how` and `why` skills and weaves what they find into one clear explanation. Use for 'teach me this', 'help me really understand X', 'explain this change or subsystem to me'.

capabilities.name: technical-writing
capabilities.description: Layered technical-writing standard: Diátaxis structure, Google developer style sentences, STE instruction rules, Global English syntax. Use for /technical-writing or when writing or reviewing docs, RFCs, readmes, PR descriptions, or commit messages.

capabilities.name: typescript-best-practices
capabilities.description: TypeScript best practices. Use when reading or editing any .ts or .tsx file.

capabilities.name: unslop
capabilities.description: Cut AI tells from any writing.

capabilities.name: why
capabilities.description: Use for 'why does X work this way', 'why we picked Y', design rationale, regressions, postmortems, or data-backed thresholds. Discovers available MCPs and queries each evidence category (source control, issue tracker, long-form docs, real-time chat, infrastructure observability, error tracking, product analytics warehouse) in parallel, then returns a cited read on decisions and tradeoffs. Use how for runtime behavior.

capabilities.name: orchestrate
capabilities.description: Use only when the user explicitly types `/orchestrate <goal>` to decompose a large task, spawn a tree of parallel cloud-agent workers/subplanners/verifiers via the Cursor SDK, and collect structured handoffs; do not invoke autonomously.

capabilities.name: reproduce-and-fix-issues
capabilities.description: Reproduce triaged Slack bugs through a configured app-control adapter, verify existing fixes, and open a bounded draft pull request only after before-and-after proof. Use only from the configured Benny repro automation.

capabilities.name: setup-benny
capabilities.description: Configure Benny and prepare its triage and repro automations. Use when installing Benny or changing its Slack, tracker, repository, routing, control, model, or budget settings.

capabilities.name: triage-issue-reports
capabilities.description: Triage Slack issue reports with one thread-only verdict, evidence review, cause-aware routing, tracker dedupe, and fail-closed ticket creation. Use only from the configured Benny triage automation.

capabilities.name: architect
capabilities.description: Sketch types, signatures, and module structure before code, then stay in the loop while implementation fills in. Use for /architect, 'architect this', 'design this', or non-trivial work where jumping to code would lock in the wrong shape.

capabilities.name: arena
capabilities.description: Spawn N parallel candidates at the same task, pick a base, graft the strongest parts of the losers into it. Use for /arena, 'arena this', 'throw it in the arena', or when one attempt at a non-trivial artifact would lock in the wrong shape.

capabilities.name: automate-me
capabilities.description: Use for \"automate me\", \"create/update/refresh my -mode skill\", \"turn/capture my preferences or working style into a skill\", or wanting agents to follow how the user works. Drafts or revises a personal -mode skill via create-skill + unslop, optionally pulling fresh evidence from recent transcripts.

capabilities.name: benchmark-checklist
capabilities.description: Vet a perf measurement (limiter, tuning, limits, errors, repeatability, relevance, and whether the work happened) before you report or act on it. Use when you run a benchmark or report a speedup or regression you measured.

capabilities.name: blast-radius
capabilities.description: Find what a change could break somewhere else before it ships, beyond the diff, and prove the one fact it's safe because of by running real code instead of writing it up. Use for 'blast radius of X', 'what could this break', or reviewing a small diff you don't trust.

capabilities.name: bro
capabilities.description: Restate the last message in plain human language, with no jargon.

capabilities.name: correct
capabilities.description: Find the mistakes agents keep repeating in this repo and make each one impossible. Try architecture first, then types, then a lint whose error names the fix, then a test, and write docs last. Prove each check fails on a real past mistake. Repeat this each time the operator corrects you. Use for /correct.

capabilities.name: create-formal-verification-skill
capabilities.description: Generate a project-local skill that formally verifies the code where a bug costs the most and tests reach the least, in any language, with whichever verification tool fits. Use for /create-formal-verification-skill, \"model-check this race\", \"prove this invariant\", or when concurrency, retries, state machines, parsers, or unsafe code need more than tests.

capabilities.name: create-verification-skill
capabilities.description: Generate a project-local verification skill that drives your app the way a user does — any language, framework, or platform. Use for /create-verification-skill, \"make a control skill for this repo\", or when a project has no scripted way to prove UI/CLI/service behavior.

capabilities.name: figure-it-out
capabilities.description: Design an auditable playbook when no narrower one fits: a large migration, an ambitious multi-part change, or work a human reviews after stepping away. Scales rigor to the task, runs a hypothesis loop, and logs decisions. Use for /figure-it-out or 'figure it out'.

capabilities.name: how
capabilities.description: Use for \"how does X work\", code walkthroughs before changing something, and placement / ownership / layering questions (\"where should this live\", \"which package owns this\", \"is this the right layer\"). Explains subsystem architecture, runtime flow, onboarding mental models. Use why for motivation.

capabilities.name: in-your-own-words
capabilities.description: Restate in your own words what you think the user's goals are and what problem they're trying to solve. Use for /in-your-own-words.

capabilities.name: interrogate
capabilities.description: Use for \"interrogate\", \"adversarial review\", \"multi-model review\", \"challenge this\", \"stress test this code\", \"find blind spots\", or \"tear this apart\". Adversaries try to break a change or design, and only findings proven by a run survive.

capabilities.name: ketchup
capabilities.description: Catch the user up on what changed in this chat since their last message, in plain words and small visuals. List every item waiting on them with what they need to decide it from the reply alone. Use for /ketchup.

capabilities.name: ketchup-video
capabilities.description: Catch the user up like /ketchup, with a short subtitled video of slides for what happened and the waiting calls as text under it. Use for /ketchup-video.

capabilities.name: maintain-formal-verification-skill
capabilities.description: Bring a project's formal verification back in line with the code after the code changes: find the commits that touched verified code, update the model, harness, or properties to describe the code as it is now, rerun, and say whether each failure is drift in the verification or a bug in the code. Use for /maintain-formal-verification-skill, \"is the model still true to the code\", or after merges and refactors that touched verified code without rechecking it.

capabilities.name: maintain-verification-skill
capabilities.description: Periodic pass that keeps a project's verification skill and feature map honest: parallel source readers per feature, one live session driving every feature, at most one PR of proven corrections. Use for /maintain-verification-skill or \"audit the verify skill\".

capabilities.name: no-comments
capabilities.description: Spawn Comment Sicko, fix accepted findings, and offer encodings for claimed constraints.

capabilities.name: poteto-help
capabilities.description: Guides users through pstack setup, /poteto-mode, and picking the skill, playbook, or principle for a task. Type /poteto-help with a question.

capabilities.name: poteto-mode
capabilities.description: poteto's agent style for concise, detailed responses, deliberate subagents, unslopped prose, simple code, and verified work. Use for poteto, /poteto-mode, or requests to work in this style.

capabilities.name: principle-attack-the-premise
capabilities.description: Apply when two or more fixes that share one premise have failed the same gate. Write the premise down and test it directly before you write another fix that assumes it.

capabilities.name: principle-boundary-discipline
capabilities.description: Apply when wiring validation, error handling, or framework adapters. Concentrate guards at system boundaries (CLI, config, network, external APIs); trust internal types and keep business logic in pure functions.

capabilities.name: principle-build-the-lever
capabilities.description: Apply to any non-trivial work, not just bulk work: edits, migrations, analyses, checks. Build the tool that does it or proves it (codemod, script, generator, or a skill your subagents follow) instead of working by hand. The tool is the artifact a reviewer can rerun.

capabilities.name: principle-encode-lessons-in-structure
capabilities.description: Apply when you catch yourself writing the same instruction a second time, or notice a recurring correction. Encode the rule as a lint, metadata flag, runtime check, or script instead of more text.

capabilities.name: principle-exhaust-the-design-space
capabilities.description: Apply when facing a novel UI interaction or architectural decision with no precedent in the codebase. Build 2-3 competing prototypes and compare side by side before committing.

capabilities.name: principle-experience-first
capabilities.description: Apply when product, UX, or feature-scope tradeoffs come up. Choose user delight over implementation convenience; ship fewer polished features over more rough ones.

capabilities.name: principle-explain-the-number
capabilities.description: Apply before you measure, and before you trust, report, or act on a number you measured: a speedup, a regression, a throughput, a latency, or an eval result. Find what limits it, and rule out that it measured something other than the work you think.

capabilities.name: principle-fix-root-causes
capabilities.description: Apply when debugging. Trace each symptom back to the first place the system went wrong and fix it there. A guard is a fix only when the state it handles is legitimate.

capabilities.name: principle-foundational-thinking
capabilities.description: Apply before writing logic: choosing core types and data structures, sequencing scaffold-vs-feature work, asking what concurrent actors share. Get the data structures right so downstream code becomes obvious.

capabilities.name: principle-guard-the-context-window
capabilities.description: Apply when context is filling up: large outputs, long files, repeated reads, fan-out planning. Route bulk to subagents; keep summaries in the main thread, not raw payloads.

capabilities.name: principle-laziness-protocol
capabilities.description: Apply when refactoring, evaluating diff size, or tempted to add abstractions, layers, or signal threading. Bias toward deletion and the smallest change that solves the problem.

capabilities.name: principle-make-operations-idempotent
capabilities.description: Apply when designing commands, lifecycle steps, or processing loops that run amid crashes, restarts, and retries. Converge to the same end state regardless of partial prior runs.

capabilities.name: principle-migrate-callers-then-delete-legacy-apis
capabilities.description: Apply when introducing a new internal API while old callers still exist. Migrate callers and delete the old API in the same wave instead of preserving compatibility layers.

capabilities.name: cancel-ralph
capabilities.description: Cancel an active Ralph Loop. Use when the user wants to stop, cancel, or abort a running ralph loop.

capabilities.name: ralph-loop
capabilities.description: Start a Ralph Loop for iterative self-referential development. Use when the user asks to run a ralph loop, start an iterative loop, or wants repeated autonomous iteration on a task until completion.

capabilities.name: ralph-loop-help
capabilities.description: Explain the Ralph Loop plugin, how it works, and available skills. Use when the user asks for help with ralph loop, wants to understand the technique, or needs usage examples.

capabilities.name: create-learning-path
capabilities.description: Build a personalized learning roadmap with milestones and practice checkpoints

capabilities.name: run-learning-retrospective
capabilities.description: Evaluate learning progress, identify blockers, and adjust the learning plan

capabilities.name: thermo-nuclear-code-quality-review
capabilities.description: Run an extremely strict maintainability review for abstraction quality, giant files, and spaghetti-condition growth. Use for a thermo-nuclear code quality review, thermonuclear review, deep code quality audit, or especially harsh maintainability review.

capabilities.name: thermo-nuclear-review
capabilities.description: Comprehensive security and correctness audit of a branch's changes. Use for thermo nuclear, thermonuclear, or deep review requests, or branch/PR diff audits focused on bugs, breaking changes, security issues, devex regressions, and feature-gate leaks.

capabilities.name: thermos
capabilities.description: Launch both thermo-nuclear review subagents in parallel, then synthesize their findings. Use for thermos, double thermo review, or combined bug/security and code-quality branch audits.

capabilities.name: google-docs
capabilities.description: Author and edit Google Docs with the google-docs tools - structured writing, character and paragraph styling, lists, tables, images, headers/footers. Use when creating a formatted document, editing document content, or applying styles.

capabilities.name: google-drive
capabilities.description: Work with Google Drive through its MCP tools - search, read, create, organize, share, comment, and export files. Use when creating files in specific folders, moving or renaming, converting Markdown/CSV into Docs/Sheets, managing comments, or exporting a rendered PDF.

capabilities.name: google-sheets
capabilities.description: Build and edit Google Sheets with the google-sheets tools - values, formatting, charts, conditional formatting, structure, validation, named and protected ranges. Use when creating a spreadsheet or dashboard, formatting cells, adding or fixing charts, or reorganizing tabs and rows.

capabilities.name: google-slides
capabilities.description: Build and edit Google Slides through the google-slides MCP tools - slides, grids of cards and columns, text boxes, shapes, images, tables, styling, layout inspection, and per-slide PNG rendering. Use when creating a deck, laying out slide elements, matching a template, or verifying how a slide looks.

capabilities.name: tailscale-setup
capabilities.description: Connect Grok Bot to Tailscale on a company tailnet (a team admin enables it at cursor.com; each member authenticates their own device and an admin limits it with custom:grokbot postures) or a personal tailnet (one-click Connect when the member owns or administers the tailnet, otherwise a tag:grokbot device). Several tailnets can be connected at once. Use when the user asks to set up, troubleshoot, change the default tailnet, or disconnect Grok Bot's Tailscale connection.
